records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר שָׁא֗וּל אֶל־יוֹנָתָ֤ן בְּנוֹ֙ וְאֶל־כָּל־עֲבָדָ֔יו לְהָמִ֖ית אֶת־דָּוִ֑ד וִיהֽוֹנָתָן֙ בֶּן־שָׁא֔וּל חָפֵ֥ץ בְּדָוִ֖ד מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And spoke Saul to Jonathan his son and to all his servants to kill David; and Jonathan son of Saul delighted in David exceedingly.
pieces: Saul spoke to his son Jonathan and to all his officials about killing David. But Saul's son Jonathan was deeply fond of David.

L.1: And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants about killing David. But Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted greatly in David.

R.1: Saul talked with his son Jonathan and all his officials about killing David. But Jonathan cared about David very much.

decisions.choice: Saul spoke about killing David: he made his plan known, and perhaps gave the order
alternatives: he ordered them to kill David
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that Saul spoke "to kill David". It can mean he told them of his intention or that he told them to do it. Until now Saul had tried to have David killed by the Philistines (18:17, 25); here for the first time he speaks openly of killing him.

decisions.choice: delighted greatly in David: took great pleasure in him, loved him
decisions.reason: The verb is used of warm approval and affection. Jonathan had already bound himself to David in friendship (18:1-4). The words "Jonathan, Saul's son" set the son against his father's plan.

decisions.choice: his servants: the men of Saul's court
decisions.reason: Here the king's servants are his officials and attendants, as in 16:15-17 and 18:22-26, not household slaves.

decisions.choice: officials (Balanced, Readable); servants (Literal)
decisions.reason: The king's servants are court officials (m3), so Balanced and Readable call them officials, as elsewhere in Samuel.

records.heading: Jonathan speaks up for David

records.source: וַיַּגֵּ֤ד יְהוֹנָתָן֙ לְדָוִ֣ד לֵאמֹ֔ר מְבַקֵּ֛שׁ שָׁא֥וּל אָבִ֖י לַהֲמִיתֶ֑ךָ וְעַתָּה֙ הִשָּֽׁמֶר־נָ֣א בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֥ בַסֵּ֖תֶר וְנַחְבֵּֽאתָ׃
records.gloss: And told Jonathan to David saying, Seeking Saul my father to kill you; and now take care please in the morning, and stay in the secret place and hide yourself.
pieces: Jonathan told David, "My father Saul is looking for a way to kill you. So please be careful in the morning. Stay in a hidden place and keep out of sight.

L.2: And Jonathan told David, saying, "Saul my father is seeking to kill you. And now, please be on your guard in the morning, and stay in a secret place and hide yourself.

R.2: Jonathan warned David. "My father Saul wants to kill you," he said. "So be careful tomorrow morning. Go to a secret place and hide there.

decisions.choice: is seeking to kill you: Saul is now actively looking for the chance
decisions.reason: The participle describes something going on at the moment of speaking: Saul's intention is fixed and he is looking for a way to carry it out.

decisions.choice: in the morning: the next morning
decisions.reason: Jonathan speaks of the morning when he will talk with his father (verse 3). David is to be hidden by then.

decisions.choice: warned; tomorrow morning
decisions.reason: Readable says "warned" for "told", since what Jonathan tells David is a warning, and makes clear that "the morning" is the next one (m2).

records.source: וַאֲנִ֨י אֵצֵ֜א וְעָמַדְתִּ֣י לְיַד־אָבִ֗י בַּשָּׂדֶה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה שָׁ֔ם וַאֲנִ֕י אֲדַבֵּ֥ר בְּךָ֖ אֶל־אָבִ֑י וְרָאִ֥יתִי מָ֖ה וְהִגַּ֥דְתִּי לָֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: And I will go out and stand at [the] side of my father in the field where you [are] there, and I will speak about you to my father, and I will see what, and I will tell you.
pieces: I will go out and take my place at my father's side in the field where you are, and talk with him about you. Whatever I find out, I will let you know."

L.3: And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you [are], and I will speak about you to my father; and [if] I see anything, I will tell you."

R.3: I will go out and stand next to my father in the field where you are hiding. I will talk to him about you. Then I will tell you whatever I learn."

decisions.choice: I will see what, and tell you: whatever I find out, I will tell you
decisions.reason: The short Hebrew phrase "see what" means to find out how things stand. Jonathan promises to pass on whatever he learns of his father's mind.

decisions.choice: the field where you are: David hides nearby
decisions.reason: Jonathan plans to meet his father in the open country close to David's hiding place, so that he can bring David word quickly. A similar plan in the field is made in 20:5, 11, 19-22.

decisions.choice: where you are hiding
decisions.reason: Readable adds "hiding" to link this with verse 2.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר יְהוֹנָתָ֤ן בְּדָוִד֙ ט֔וֹב אֶל־שָׁא֖וּל אָבִ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵ֠לָיו אַל־יֶחֱטָ֨א הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ בְּעַבְדּ֣וֹ בְדָוִ֗ד כִּ֣י ל֤וֹא חָטָא֙ לָ֔ךְ וְכִ֥י מַעֲשָׂ֖יו טוֹב־לְךָ֥ מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And spoke Jonathan of David good to Saul his father and said to him, Not let sin the king against his servant, against David, because not he has sinned against you, and because his deeds [are] good to you exceedingly.
pieces: Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul. "May the king not sin against David his servant," he said. "David has committed no sin against you, and what he has done has served you very well.

L.4: And Jonathan spoke good of David to Saul his father, and said to him, "Let not the king sin against his servant, against David, for he has not sinned against you, and for his deeds [have been] very good toward you.

R.4: Jonathan said good things about David to his father Saul. He told him, "Do not sin against David, who serves you. He has not sinned against you. In fact, everything he has done has been a great help to you.

decisions.choice: let not the king sin: a son speaking to his father as a subject to his king
decisions.reason: Jonathan speaks of Saul as "the king" rather than "you", the respectful way to address a ruler, and frames his plea as a warning against sin.

decisions.choice: sin against: wrong someone who has done no wrong
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice: Saul would be sinning against David, while David has not sinned against Saul. Killing a loyal and innocent man would be a sin (verse 5).

decisions.choice: his servant: David as one who serves the king
decisions.reason: David is Saul's servant in the sense of his loyal officer and commander (18:5, 13), not a slave.

decisions.choice: Do not sin against David, who serves you
decisions.reason: Readable turns the courtly "the king" into a direct "you" (m1), and says "who serves you" for "his servant" (m3).

records.source: וַיָּשֶׂם֩ אֶת־נַפְשׁ֨וֹ בְכַפּ֜וֹ וַיַּ֣ךְ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֗י וַיַּ֨עַשׂ יְהוָ֜ה תְּשׁוּעָ֤ה גְדוֹלָה֙ לְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רָאִ֖יתָ וַתִּשְׂמָ֑ח וְלָ֤מָּה תֶֽחֱטָא֙ בְּדָ֣ם נָקִ֔י לְהָמִ֥ית אֶת־דָּוִ֖ד חִנָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And he put his life in his palm and struck the Philistine, and made Yahweh a deliverance great for all Israel; you saw and you rejoiced. And why will you sin against blood innocent by killing David without cause?
pieces: He took his life in his hands and struck down the Philistine, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} won a great victory for all Israel. You saw it and were glad. So why would you sin against innocent blood by putting David to death for no reason?"

L.5: And he put his life in his palm and struck down the Philistine, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} worked a great deliverance for all Israel. You saw [it] and rejoiced. And why will you sin against innocent blood by killing David without cause?"

R.5: He risked his life when he killed Goliath the Philistine, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave all Israel a great victory. You saw it, and you were happy. So why would you sin by killing David? He is innocent, and there is no reason to kill him."

decisions.choice: put his life in his palm: risked his life
decisions.reason: To hold one's life in one's hand is to put it at risk, as something that could easily be lost (Judges 12:3; 1 Samuel 28:21).

decisions.choice: the Philistine: Goliath
decisions.reason: Jonathan points to David's fight with Goliath of Gath (17:4, 48-51), which Saul himself watched.

decisions.choice: the LORD worked a great deliverance: the victory was Yahweh's
decisions.reason: David had said before the fight that the battle belonged to Yahweh (17:47). Jonathan reminds Saul that through David God rescued the whole nation.

decisions.choice: sin against innocent blood: bring guilt by killing an innocent man
decisions.reason: Shedding the blood of someone who has done nothing worthy of death brings guilt on the one who does it (Deuteronomy 19:10; 21:8-9). "Without cause" stresses that David has given no reason.

decisions.choice: won a great victory (Balanced); gave all Israel a great victory (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means rescue or deliverance; in a battle it is the victory itself, so Balanced and Readable say "victory". Literal keeps "deliverance".

decisions.choice: Goliath the Philistine; He is innocent
decisions.reason: Readable names Goliath (m2) and makes "innocent blood" into a plain statement about David.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע שָׁא֖וּל בְּק֣וֹל יְהוֹנָתָ֑ן וַיִּשָּׁבַ֣ע שָׁא֔וּל חַי־יְהוָ֖ה אִם־יוּמָֽת׃
records.gloss: And listened Saul to [the] voice of Jonathan, and swore Saul, [As] lives Yahweh, if he will be put to death.
pieces: Saul listened to Jonathan and swore, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, he will not be put to death."

L.6: And Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul swore, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, he shall not be put to death."

R.6: Saul listened to Jonathan. He made a solemn promise: "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, David will not be killed."

decisions.choice: As the LORD lives, if he is put to death: he will certainly not be put to death
decisions.reason: This is the form of an oath. "As Yahweh lives" calls on the living God as witness, and "if he is put to death" leaves unspoken the curse the speaker accepts if it happens; so it is a strong promise that it will not happen (14:39, 45).

decisions.choice: listened to the voice of: did what Jonathan urged
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to heed and accept what they say.

decisions.choice: will not (Balanced, Readable); shall not with [As] supplied (Literal)
decisions.reason: English has no oath form with "if" that means "not", so every level gives the sense (m1). Readable names David for clarity.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֤א יְהוֹנָתָן֙ לְדָוִ֔ד וַיַּגֶּד־לוֹ֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיָּבֵ֨א יְהוֹנָתָ֤ן אֶת־דָּוִד֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל וַיְהִ֥י לְפָנָ֖יו כְּאֶתְמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃ס
records.gloss: And called Jonathan to David, and told to him Jonathan all the words these; and brought Jonathan David to Saul, and he was before him as yesterday [and] three days ago.
pieces: Then Jonathan called David and told him everything that had been said. Jonathan brought David to Saul, and David served him as he had before.

L.7: And Jonathan called David, and Jonathan told him all these words. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was before him as yesterday [and the day] before.

R.7: Then Jonathan called David and told him all about it. He brought David back to Saul, and David served Saul as he had done before.

decisions.choice: as yesterday and the day before: as in the past
decisions.reason: "Yesterday and three days ago" is a Hebrew way of saying "formerly", "as before" (Genesis 31:2; Exodus 5:7).

decisions.choice: he was before him: he was in Saul's service again
decisions.reason: To be before a king is to stand in his presence as one who serves him (16:21-22). David returns to his place at court.

decisions.choice: served him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what being "before him" meant (m2). Readable adds "back" since David had been in hiding.

records.source: וַתּ֥וֹסֶף הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה לִֽהְי֑וֹת וַיֵּצֵ֨א דָוִ֜ד וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיַּ֤ךְ בָּהֶם֙ מַכָּ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ מִפָּנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And again the war was, and went out David and fought against Philistines, and struck them a blow great, and they fled from before him.
pieces: War broke out again. David went out and fought the Philistines. He defeated them with heavy losses, and they ran from him.

L.8: And there was war again, and David went out and fought against [the] Philistines, and struck them [with] a great blow, and they fled from before him.

R.8: Once again there was war. David went out and fought the Philistines. He beat them badly, and they ran away from him.

decisions.choice: struck them a great blow: defeated them with great loss of life
decisions.reason: "Striking a great blow" is the usual way of describing a heavy defeat in battle (Joshua 10:10; Judges 11:33).

decisions.choice: David's success brings back Saul's jealousy
decisions.reason: Each victory of David had made Saul more afraid of him (18:5-9, 14-16, 30). The next verse shows the same pattern again.

records.source: וַתְּהִי֩ ר֨וּחַ יְהוָ֤ה׀רָעָה֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל וְהוּא֙ בְּבֵית֣וֹ יוֹשֵׁ֔ב וַחֲנִית֖וֹ בְּיָד֑וֹ וְדָוִ֖ד מְנַגֵּ֥ן בְּיָֽד׃
records.gloss: And was a spirit of Yahweh evil upon Saul, and he in his house [was] sitting, and his spear in his hand, and David [was] playing with hand.
pieces: Then an evil spirit from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on Saul. He was sitting in his house, spear in hand, while David played the lyre.

L.9: And an evil spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on Saul as he was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand, and David was playing with [his] hand.

R.9: Then an evil spirit from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on Saul. He was sitting at home, holding his spear, and David was playing the lyre for him.

decisions.choice: an evil spirit of the LORD: a troubling spirit sent by Yahweh
decisions.reason: The phrase is the same in sense as "an evil spirit from Yahweh" in 16:14. After the Spirit of Yahweh left Saul (16:14), a spirit that tormented him came by God's permission and as his judgment, as in Judges 9:23. The text does not say more about what this spirit was.

decisions.choice: evil: harmful, troubling
decisions.reason: The word can describe something morally evil or something that does harm or brings distress. Here its effect is Saul's dark moods and violent anger.

decisions.choice: the spear and the music: the scene of 18:10-11 again
decisions.reason: David was first brought to court to play for Saul when the spirit troubled him (16:16, 23). Once before, while David played, Saul hurled his spear at him (18:10-11).

decisions.choice: playing with his hand: playing a stringed instrument
decisions.reason: The verb means to play a stringed instrument by plucking it. The instrument David played for Saul is the lyre of 16:16, 23.

decisions.choice: an evil spirit from the LORD; playing the lyre
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "from the LORD", as in 16:14, since the sense is the same (m1); Literal keeps "of". They name the instrument from 16:16 (m4).

records.source: וַיְבַקֵּ֨שׁ שָׁא֜וּל לְהַכּ֤וֹת בַּֽחֲנִית֙ בְּדָוִ֣ד וּבַקִּ֔יר וַיִּפְטַר֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶֽת־הַחֲנִ֖ית בַּקִּ֑יר וְדָוִ֛ד נָ֥ס וַיִּמָּלֵ֖ט בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הֽוּא׃פ
records.gloss: And sought Saul to strike with the spear into David and into the wall, and he slipped away from before Saul, and he struck the spear into the wall; and David fled and escaped in the night that.
pieces: Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David slipped away from him, and Saul drove the spear into the wall. David fled and got away that night.

L.10: And Saul sought to strike David and the wall with the spear, but he slipped away from before Saul, and he struck the spear into the wall. And David fled and escaped that night.

R.10: Saul tried to nail David to the wall with his spear. But David moved out of the way, and Saul's spear went into the wall. That night David ran away and escaped.

decisions.choice: to strike into David and into the wall: to pin David to the wall
decisions.reason: Saul meant to drive the spear through David and into the wall behind him, as in 18:11.

decisions.choice: that night: the end of David's escape, not the start of verse 11
decisions.reason: The Hebrew accents put "that night" with David's escape. The old Greek translation joins it to the next verse ("that night Saul sent messengers"). Either way, the events of verses 11-17 happen the same night.

decisions.choice: pin (Balanced); nail (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Strike David and the wall" is put in words that show the picture plainly (m1).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ שָׁא֨וּל מַלְאָכִ֜ים אֶל־בֵּ֤ית דָּוִד֙ לְשָׁמְר֔וֹ וְלַהֲמִית֖וֹ בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַתַּגֵּ֣ד לְדָוִ֗ד מִיכַ֤ל אִשְׁתּוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אִם־אֵ֨ינְךָ֜ מְמַלֵּ֤ט אֶֽת־נַפְשְׁךָ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה מָחָ֖ר אַתָּ֥ה מוּמָֽת׃
records.gloss: And sent Saul messengers to [the] house of David to watch him and to kill him in the morning; and told David Michal his wife saying, If not you [are] saving your life tonight, tomorrow you [are] put to death.
pieces: Saul sent messengers to David's house to keep watch on him and kill him in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, warned him, "If you do not escape with your life tonight, tomorrow you will be dead."

L.11: And Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch him and to kill him in the morning. But Michal his wife told David, saying, "If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you will be put to death."

R.11: Saul sent men to David's house. They were to watch him through the night and kill him in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, warned him. "If you do not run for your life tonight," she said, "tomorrow you will be killed."

decisions.choice: Michal his wife: Saul's daughter
decisions.reason: Michal was Saul's younger daughter, who loved David and was given to him in marriage (14:49; 18:20-27). She now takes her husband's side against her father.

decisions.choice: to watch him and kill him in the morning: wait until daylight to kill him
decisions.reason: The messengers guard the house through the night so that David cannot leave, and are to kill him in the morning, perhaps when he comes out (compare Judges 16:2).

decisions.choice: men
decisions.reason: Readable calls the messengers "men": they are Saul's agents sent to do his will, not only to carry a message.

records.heading: Michal helps David escape

records.source: וַתֹּ֧רֶד מִיכַ֛ל אֶת־דָּוִ֖ד בְּעַ֣ד הַחַלּ֑וֹן וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ וַיִּבְרַ֖ח וַיִּמָּלֵֽט׃
records.gloss: And let down Michal David through the window, and he went and fled and escaped.
pieces: So Michal let David down through the window, and he went off, fled, and escaped.

L.12: And Michal let David down through the window, and he went and fled and escaped.

R.12: So Michal let David down out of a window, and he ran away and escaped.

decisions.choice: let down through the window: an escape past those guarding the door
decisions.reason: The watchers are at the door, so David leaves by a window, as the spies escaped from Jericho (Joshua 2:15). The text does not say how she let him down, but a rope is likely.

decisions.choice: went and fled and escaped: three verbs for one swift escape
decisions.reason: The three verbs piled together stress that David got clean away.

records.source: וַתִּקַּ֨ח מִיכַ֜ל אֶת־הַתְּרָפִ֗ים וַתָּ֨שֶׂם֙ אֶל־הַמִּטָּ֔ה וְאֵת֙ כְּבִ֣יר הָֽעִזִּ֔ים שָׂ֖מָה מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָ֑יו וַתְּכַ֖ס בַּבָּֽגֶד׃ס
records.gloss: And took Michal the teraphim and put [it] on the bed, and [the] net of the goats she put [at] its head-place, and covered [it] with the garment.
pieces: Then Michal took the household god and laid it on the bed. She put a mat of goats' hair at its head and covered it with a garment.

L.13: And Michal took the household gods and laid [it] on the bed, and she put the mat of goats' [hair] at its head, and covered [it] with the garment.

R.13: Then Michal took the household idol and laid it in the bed. She put goat hair at the head and covered it with a piece of clothing.

decisions.choice: teraphim: a household god, here one figure the size of a man
decisions.reason: The teraphim were figures of gods kept in a home, perhaps to protect it or to give guidance (Genesis 31:19, 34; Judges 17:5). The word is plural in form but here means a single figure, large enough to look like a man lying in bed; Rachel's were small enough to hide in a saddle (Genesis 31:34). The text does not explain why there was one in David's house; later such things are condemned (15:23; 2 Kings 23:24).

decisions.choice: the mat of goats' hair: something of goat hair at its head, to look like a person's hair
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here and in verse 16, so its sense is uncertain. It may be a woven mat or net of goat hair, a pillow stuffed with it, or a cover. Its purpose is clear: dark goat hair at the head made the figure look like a sleeping man.

decisions.choice: the garment: a cloak used as a blanket
decisions.reason: The outer cloak served as a covering at night (Exodus 22:25-26).

decisions.choice: the household gods (Literal); the household god (Balanced); the household idol (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plural form with the settled term "household gods"; Balanced and Readable use the singular, since one figure is meant (m1), and Readable says "idol" as the book's term list does. A small idol, as in Genesis 31:19, would not fit here.

decisions.choice: goat hair
decisions.reason: Readable keeps only what is certain about the object (m2).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח שָׁא֛וּל מַלְאָכִ֖ים לָקַ֣חַת אֶת־דָּוִ֑ד וַתֹּ֖אמֶר חֹלֶ֥ה הֽוּא׃פ
records.gloss: And sent Saul messengers to take David, and she said, Sick [is] he.
pieces: When Saul sent messengers to seize David, she said, "He is sick."

L.14: And Saul sent messengers to take David, and she said, "He [is] sick."

R.14: When Saul's men came to take David away, Michal told them, "He is sick."

decisions.choice: sent messengers to take David: in the morning, to arrest him
decisions.reason: This seems to be the morning of verse 11, when the watchers were to take David. Michal plays for time so that David can get further away.

decisions.choice: Michal told them
decisions.reason: Readable names Michal and the people she speaks to.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים לִרְא֥וֹת אֶת־דָּוִ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הַעֲל֨וּ אֹת֧וֹ בַמִּטָּ֛ה אֵלַ֖י לַהֲמִתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And sent Saul the messengers to see David saying, Bring up him in the bed to me to kill him.
pieces: Then Saul sent the messengers back to see David for themselves. He told them, "Bring him up to me in his bed, so that I can kill him."

L.15: And Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, "Bring him up to me in the bed, to kill him."

R.15: Saul sent the men back to see David with their own eyes. He ordered them, "Carry him to me in his bed so I can kill him."

decisions.choice: sent the messengers to see David: sent them back to look at him themselves
decisions.reason: "The messengers" with the article are the same men, sent again to see whether David was really sick.

decisions.choice: bring him up in the bed: carry him on his bed or mat
decisions.reason: A bed could be a light frame or mat that could be carried. "Up" may reflect that Saul's house in Gibeah stood higher, or simply going up to the king.

decisions.choice: back; for themselves; so that I can kill him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that these are the same messengers sent again (m1), and that Saul means to kill David himself.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַתְּרָפִ֖ים אֶל־הַמִּטָּ֑ה וּכְבִ֥יר הָעִזִּ֖ים מְרַאֲשֹׁתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And came the messengers, and look, the teraphim on the bed, and [the] net of the goats [at] its head-place.
pieces: When the messengers came in, there was the household god on the bed, with the mat of goats' hair at its head.

L.16: And the messengers came, and look, the household gods [were] on the bed, with the mat of goats' [hair] at its head.

R.16: When the men came in, they saw that it was the household idol in the bed, with goat hair at its head.

decisions.choice: look: the messengers' surprise
decisions.reason: The word draws the reader into what the messengers saw as they pulled back the cover: not David, but the household god.

decisions.choice: household gods / household god / household idol; mat of goats' hair
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל־מִיכַ֗ל לָ֤מָּה כָּ֨כָה֙ רִמִּיתִ֔נִי וַתְּשַׁלְּחִ֥י אֶת־אֹיְבִ֖י וַיִּמָּלֵ֑ט וַתֹּ֤אמֶר מִיכַל֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל הוּא־אָמַ֥ר אֵלַ֛י שַׁלְּחִ֖נִי לָמָ֥ה אֲמִיתֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And said Saul to Michal, Why thus have you deceived me, and you let go my enemy, and he escaped? And said Michal to Saul, He said to me, Let me go; why should I kill you?
pieces: Saul said to Michal, "Why did you trick me like this and let my enemy go, so that he got away?" Michal answered, "He told me, 'Let me go! Why should I have to kill you?'"

L.17: And Saul said to Michal, "Why have you deceived me like this, and let my enemy go, so that he has escaped?" And Michal said to Saul, "He said to me, 'Let me go. Why should I kill you?'"

R.17: Saul asked Michal, "Why did you fool me like this? You let my enemy get away!" Michal answered, "He told me, 'Let me go, or I will kill you!'"

decisions.choice: my enemy: Saul now openly calls David his enemy
decisions.reason: The writer had said that Saul became David's enemy (18:29); now Saul says it of his own son-in-law to his daughter.

decisions.choice: Why should I kill you? A threat: let me go, or I will kill you
decisions.reason: The question is a way of threatening. Michal claims that David forced her to help him, to protect herself from her father's anger. The reader knows from verses 11-12 that she acted on her own.

decisions.choice: Let me go, or I will kill you!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the threatening question into the plain threat it implies (m2).

records.source: וְדָוִ֨ד בָּרַ֜ח וַיִּמָּלֵ֗ט וַיָּבֹ֤א אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל֙ הָרָמָ֔תָה וַיַּ֨גֶּד־ל֔וֹ אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָֽשָׂה־ל֖וֹ שָׁא֑וּל וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הוּא֙ וּשְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ בְּנָֽיוֹת׃
records.gloss: And David fled and escaped, and came to Samuel to Ramah, and told to him all that had done to him Saul; and went he and Samuel and they stayed at Naioth.
pieces: So David fled and escaped. He went to Samuel at Ramah and reported to him everything Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel went off and stayed at Naioth.

L.18: And David fled and escaped, and he came to Samuel at Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and stayed at Naioth.

R.18: David ran away and got safely to Samuel at Ramah. He told Samuel everything Saul had done to him. Then David and Samuel went to Naioth and stayed there.

decisions.choice: Ramah: Samuel's home town
decisions.reason: Samuel lived at Ramah, where he judged Israel and built an altar (7:17; 15:34; 16:13). David runs to the prophet who had anointed him (16:13).

decisions.choice: Naioth: the form read aloud, as the margin directs
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell the name slightly differently; the vowels and the marginal note give "Naioth". The same happens in verses 19, 22 and 23. It is the same place either way.

decisions.choice: Naioth: a place in or near Ramah, perhaps meaning "dwellings"
decisions.reason: The name may mean "dwellings" or "camps", and some take it to be the quarters where Samuel's group of prophets lived (verse 20) rather than a town. It is always "Naioth in Ramah" (verses 19, 22, 23).

records.source: וַיֻּגַּ֥ד לְשָׁא֖וּל לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה דָוִ֔ד בְּנָי֖וֹת בָּרָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was told to Saul saying, Look David [is] at Naioth in Ramah.
pieces: Saul was told, "David is at Naioth in Ramah."

L.19: And it was told to Saul, saying, "Look, David [is] at Naioth in Ramah."

R.19: Someone told Saul, "David is at Naioth in Ramah."

decisions.choice: it was told to Saul: someone reported it
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the informer unnamed; David is hard to hide from Saul's informers (23:19; 26:1).

decisions.choice: "look" left out (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word that calls attention to the news is kept at Literal; Balanced and Readable let the news itself carry it.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח שָׁא֣וּל מַלְאָכִים֮ לָקַ֣חַת אֶת־דָּוִד֒ וַיַּ֗רְא אֶֽת־לַהֲקַ֤ת הַנְּבִיאִים֙ נִבְּאִ֔ים וּשְׁמוּאֵ֕ל עֹמֵ֥ד נִצָּ֖ב עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַתְּהִ֞י עַֽל־מַלְאֲכֵ֤י שָׁאוּל֙ ר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ גַּם־הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: And sent Saul messengers to take David, and he saw the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing, stationed over them; and was upon [the] messengers of Saul [the] Spirit of God, and they prophesied, also they.
pieces: Saul sent messengers to seize David. But when they saw the company of prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing there as their leader, the Spirit of God came on Saul's messengers, and they also prophesied.

L.20: And Saul sent messengers to take David. And he saw the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing, stationed over them; and the Spirit of God came on Saul's messengers, and they also prophesied.

R.20: So Saul sent men to arrest David. They saw a group of prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing there as their leader. Then the Spirit of God came on Saul's men, and they began prophesying too.

decisions.choice: he saw: the band of messengers saw, taken as one
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is singular, "he saw", though messengers were sent. It may treat the group as one, or point to its leader. The old Greek and other early translations have "they saw"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: company: a band or assembly of prophets
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It seems to be a form of the common word for an assembly, and the sense "group" fits the context.

decisions.choice: prophesying: speaking and acting under the power of God's Spirit
decisions.reason: Here prophesying is not foretelling but a state of inspired speech and praise, sometimes with music and strong excitement, as with the prophets Saul met in 10:5-6, 10 and the elders in Numbers 11:25-27.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God came on Saul's messengers: God himself stops them
decisions.reason: The men sent to seize David are overcome by God's Spirit and cannot carry out their orders. God protects David without any human help.

decisions.choice: they saw (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: English needs a plural after "messengers"; the sense is the same (m1).

decisions.choice: as their leader
decisions.reason: "Stationed over them" means Samuel was in charge of the group.

records.source: וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ לְשָׁא֗וּל וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ מַלְאָכִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ גַּם־הֵ֑מָּה וַיֹּ֣סֶף שָׁא֗וּל וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ מַלְאָכִ֣ים שְׁלִשִׁ֔ים וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ גַּם־הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: And they told Saul, and he sent messengers other, and they prophesied also they; and again Saul sent messengers third, and they prophesied also they.
pieces: When Saul was told, he sent other messengers, and they prophesied too. Saul sent messengers a third time, and they also prophesied.

L.21: And they told Saul, and he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Saul again sent messengers, a third [group], and they also prophesied.

R.21: When Saul heard about this, he sent more men, and they also began prophesying. Saul sent men a third time, and they prophesied too.

decisions.choice: they told Saul: it was reported to him
decisions.reason: "They" is impersonal: someone brought the news.

decisions.choice: three groups of messengers, each stopped the same way
decisions.reason: The threefold sending, each ending with "they also prophesied", shows that Saul's efforts are useless against God, as with the three groups sent to Elijah (2 Kings 1:9-13).

records.source: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ גַּם־ה֜וּא הָרָמָ֗תָה וַיָּבֹא֙ עַד־בּ֤וֹר הַגָּדוֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשֶּׂ֔כוּ וַיִּשְׁאַ֣ל וַיֹּ֔אמֶר אֵיפֹ֥ה שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל וְדָוִ֑ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֖ה בְּנָי֥וֹת בָּרָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And went also he to Ramah, and came to [the] cistern the great which [is] in Secu, and asked and said, Where [are] Samuel and David? And said, Look, at Naioth in Ramah.
pieces: Then Saul himself went to Ramah. He came to the great cistern at Secu and asked, "Where are Samuel and David?" Someone said, "They are at Naioth in Ramah."

L.22: And he also went to Ramah, and came to the great cistern that [is] in Secu. And he asked and said, "Where [are] Samuel and David?" And [someone] said, "Look, at Naioth in Ramah."

R.22: At last Saul went to Ramah himself. When he came to the large water cistern at Secu, he asked, "Where are Samuel and David?" Someone told him, "They are at Naioth in Ramah."

decisions.choice: the great cistern: a large pit dug to store rainwater
decisions.reason: Cisterns cut into the rock held the winter rain. A large one would be a known landmark and a place where people gathered to draw water.

decisions.choice: Secu: a place near Ramah, otherwise unknown
decisions.reason: The name appears only here. The old Greek translation reads differently here (something like "on the bare height"), which suggests a different reading of the same consonants. The Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: and he said: someone answered
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it means that someone answered him.

decisions.choice: Saul himself; Someone; They are
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Saul, give the unnamed speaker as "someone", and complete the short answer.

records.source: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שָׁ֔ם אֶל־נָי֖וֹת בָּרָמָ֑ה וַתְּהִי֩ עָלָ֨יו גַּם־ה֜וּא ר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֗ים וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הָלוֹךְ֙ וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֔א עַד־בֹּא֖וֹ בְּנָי֥וֹת בָּרָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he went there to Naioth in Ramah, and was upon him also him [the] Spirit of God, and he went, going and prophesying, until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
pieces: So he went there, toward Naioth in Ramah. The Spirit of God came on him too, and he kept walking along, prophesying, until he came to Naioth in Ramah.

L.23: And he went there to Naioth in Ramah, and the Spirit of God came on him also, and he went on walking and prophesying until he came to Naioth in Ramah.

R.23: So Saul headed for Naioth in Ramah. But on the way the Spirit of God came on him too. He kept on prophesying as he walked, all the way to Naioth in Ramah.

decisions.choice: he went, going and prophesying: he kept walking and prophesying the whole way
decisions.reason: The repeated verb of going shows something continuing; Saul prophesies all along the road.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God came on Saul himself: God stops him before he reaches David
decisions.reason: Like his messengers, Saul is overcome before he can do anything to David.

decisions.choice: the Spirit came on Saul at the start of his reign too
decisions.reason: When Saul was first anointed, the Spirit of God came on him and he prophesied among the prophets (10:6, 10). Then it was a sign of God's favor; now it holds him back from his purpose.

decisions.choice: toward (Balanced); headed for, on the way (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verse says he set out for Naioth and then that he came to it, so Balanced and Readable make clear that the Spirit came on him on the road.

records.source: וַיִּפְשַׁ֨ט גַּם־ה֜וּא בְּגָדָ֗יו וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֤א גַם־הוּא֙ לִפְנֵ֣י שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיִּפֹּ֣ל עָרֹ֔ם כָּל־הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וְכָל־הַלָּ֑יְלָה עַל־כֵּן֙ יֹֽאמְר֔וּ הֲגַ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל בַּנְּבִיאִֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And stripped off also he his clothes, and prophesied also he before Samuel, and fell naked all the day that and all the night; therefore they say, [Is] also Saul among the prophets?
pieces: He too stripped off his clothes, and he too prophesied in Samuel's presence. He lay there naked all that day and all that night. That is why people say, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"

L.24: And he also stripped off his clothes, and he also prophesied before Samuel, and he fell [down] naked all that day and all that night. Therefore they say, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"

R.24: Like the others, Saul took off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He lay there naked all that day and all that night. That is why people say, "Is even Saul one of the prophets?"

decisions.choice: naked: stripped of his outer clothes, perhaps fully
decisions.reason: The word can mean completely naked or wearing only an undergarment (Isaiah 20:2-3). Either way Saul lies stripped of his royal clothing, overcome and helpless.

decisions.choice: fell: lay down, collapsed
decisions.reason: Saul fell to the ground and lay there under the power of the Spirit.

decisions.choice: Is Saul also among the prophets? The saying of 10:11-12
decisions.reason: The same saying first arose when Saul prophesied at Gibeah (10:11-12). Here it is heard again. Then it marked a surprise at the start of his reign; now it shows the king brought low before Samuel.

decisions.choice: stripping off his clothes: the king's robe laid aside
decisions.reason: Clothing marks Saul's rule in the story: Samuel's robe tore as the kingdom was torn from Saul (15:27-28), and Jonathan gave his robe to David (18:4). The text does not say that Saul's stripping is a sign, but it fits that pattern.

decisions.choice: Like the others
decisions.reason: Readable gathers the two "also he" phrases, which compare Saul with his messengers, into one phrase at the start.
